info.name: OpenSERP API
Search
Search web results from a specific engine

params.name: engine
params.description: Search engine endpoint alias (`duck` is DuckDuckGo).

params.name: text
params.description: Search query text. At least one of `text`, `site`, or `file` must be non-empty.

params.name: lang
params.description: Language code (engine-specific behavior).

params.name: region
params.description: Market/location hint. Country or locale-style values such as `US`, `DE`, or `en-GB` are shared by engines that support them. Google also accepts city names such as `Berlin` or `New York` and sends them as `uule`. Yandex accepts numeric `lr` region IDs such as `213`; those IDs are engine-specific and are ignored by other engines.

params.name: date
params.description: Date interval in `YYYYMMDD..YYYYMMDD` format.

params.name: file
params.description: File extension filter (for engines that support it).

params.name: site
params.description: Site/domain filter.

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum organic results to return (1-100). Ads may be returned in addition. Omitted or small limits (<=10) parse only the first SERP page; larger limits may paginate when an engine supports it.

params.name: start
params.description: Pagination offset (must be >= 0).

params.name: filter
params.description: Duplicate filtering flag (primarily used by Google parser behavior).

params.name: features
params.description: Populate the top-level serp_features array (AI summaries, answer boxes, people-also-ask, related searches) from the live browser search when supported by the engine.

params.name: extract
params.description: Fetch and embed cleaned target-page content for the top web results. Accepts a boolean or an integer depth: `extract=0`/`false` disables extraction; `extract=true`/`1` enriches the top result; `extract=N` (1-5) enriches the top N results. The tuning params `extract_mode` and `min_runes` imply `extract=true` (top 1) when present, unless `extract=0` is set explicitly.

params.name: extract_mode
params.description: Extraction strategy for target pages. Its presence implies `extract=true` unless `extract=0` is set explicitly.

params.name: min_runes
params.description: Auto-mode escalation floor: if the fast (raw) pass yields fewer extracted-text runes than this, escalate to a browser render. `0` (default) uses the built-in floor. Ignored in `fast` and `rendered` modes.

params.name: format
params.description: Output format. `json` (default) returns the envelope. `markdown` returns a Markdown document suitable for Slack/email. `text` returns a minimal plain-text block optimised for LLM context windows. `ndjson` returns one result object per line with no envelope. The `Accept` header is also checked (`text/markdown`, `text/plain`, `application/x-ndjson`).

items.docs: Engine path values are `google`, `yandex`, `baidu`, `bing`, `duck`, and `ecosia` (`duck` maps to DuckDuckGo internally). Use `?format=markdown|text|ndjson` for alternative output formats.

info.name: Parse a Google SERP HTML document into structured results

params.name: format
params.description: Output format. `json` (default) returns the envelope. `markdown` returns a Markdown document suitable for Slack/email. `text` returns a minimal plain-text block optimised for LLM context windows. `ndjson` returns one result object per line with no envelope. The `Accept` header is also checked (`text/markdown`, `text/plain`, `application/x-ndjson`).

items.docs: Accepts raw Google SERP HTML in the request body and returns a standard search envelope. Useful when an upstream provider delivers raw HTML rather than JSON. No browser is used; parsing is done with goquery. The body size limit is 10 MB.

info.name: Extract clean content from one URL

params.name: url
params.description: Absolute URL to fetch and extract.

params.name: mode
params.description: Extraction strategy for one URL.

params.name: min_runes
params.description: Auto-mode escalation floor: if the fast (raw) pass yields fewer extracted-text runes than this, escalate to a browser render. `0` (default) uses the built-in floor. Ignored in `fast` and `rendered` modes.

params.name: lang
params.description: Language code (engine-specific behavior).

params.name: clean
params.description: Article-only extraction (default). Set `false` for whole-readable-body extraction that keeps nav/feature/landing content trafilatura would otherwise strip — useful for landing pages, doc indexes, and dashboards.

params.name: use_llms_txt
params.description: When the URL is a site root, probe `/llms-full.txt` then `/llms.txt` and return that LLM-optimized markdown instead of scraping HTML (see https://llmstxt.org/). Falls through to normal extraction when absent. Ignored for non-root URLs, where it would miss the requested page's own content.

params.name: format
params.description: Output format. `json` (default) returns the envelope. `markdown` returns a Markdown document suitable for Slack/email. `text` returns a minimal plain-text block optimised for LLM context windows. `ndjson` returns one result object per line with no envelope. The `Accept` header is also checked (`text/markdown`, `text/plain`, `application/x-ndjson`).

info.name: Extract content from multiple URLs

items.docs: Accepts up to 20 URLs (deduplicated) and returns a bare JSON array of `{page_content, metadata}` items - the shape Open WebUI's external web loader expects. A URL that fails validation or extraction yields an item with `metadata.error` and an empty `page_content` instead of failing the batch. `400` is reserved for malformed requests: empty or oversized `urls`, unknown `mode`, invalid proxy headers.

Search across multiple engines with selectable execution mode

params.name: text
params.description: Search query text. At least one of `text`, `site`, or `file` must be non-empty.

params.name: lang
params.description: Language code (engine-specific behavior).

params.name: region
params.description: Market/location hint. Country or locale-style values such as `US`, `DE`, or `en-GB` are shared by engines that support them. Google also accepts city names such as `Berlin` or `New York` and sends them as `uule`. Yandex accepts numeric `lr` region IDs such as `213`; those IDs are engine-specific and are ignored by other engines.

params.name: date
params.description: Date interval in `YYYYMMDD..YYYYMMDD` format.

params.name: file
params.description: File extension filter (for engines that support it).

params.name: site
params.description: Site/domain filter.

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum organic results to return (1-100). Ads may be returned in addition. Omitted or small limits (<=10) parse only the first SERP page; larger limits may paginate when an engine supports it.

params.description: Pagination offset (must be >= 0).

params.name: features
params.description: Populate the top-level serp_features array (AI summaries, answer boxes, people-also-ask, related searches) from the live browser search when supported by the engine.

params.name: engines
params.description: Comma-separated engine list for mega endpoints. If omitted, all available engines are used.

params.name: mode
params.description: Mega execution mode. `balanced` (default) runs all selected engines in parallel. `any` runs selected engines sequentially in request order until first success. `fast` runs only one engine: the fastest by circuit-breaker average response time.

params.name: dedupe
params.description: Enable deduplication by normalized URL. Default `true`.

params.name: merge
params.description: Merge results from all successful engines into one flat list. Default `true`. When `false`, only the first requested engine that returned results is kept.

params.name: extract
params.description: Fetch and embed cleaned target-page content for the top web results. Accepts a boolean or an integer depth: `extract=0`/`false` disables extraction; `extract=true`/`1` enriches the top result; `extract=N` (1-5) enriches the top N results. The tuning params `extract_mode` and `min_runes` imply `extract=true` (top 1) when present, unless `extract=0` is set explicitly.

params.name: extract_mode
params.description: Extraction strategy for target pages. Its presence implies `extract=true` unless `extract=0` is set explicitly.

params.name: min_runes
params.description: Auto-mode escalation floor: if the fast (raw) pass yields fewer extracted-text runes than this, escalate to a browser render. `0` (default) uses the built-in floor. Ignored in `fast` and `rendered` modes.

params.name: format
params.description: Output format. `json` (default) returns the envelope. `markdown` returns a Markdown document suitable for Slack/email. `text` returns a minimal plain-text block optimised for LLM context windows. `ndjson` returns one result object per line with no envelope. The `Accept` header is also checked (`text/markdown`, `text/plain`, `application/x-ndjson`).

items.docs: Mode controls engine execution strategy: `balanced` (default) queries all selected engines in parallel, `any` runs engines sequentially in requested order until first success, and `fast` queries only the fastest engine based on circuit-breaker average response time stats. In `balanced` mode, `dedupe` and `merge` tune aggregation behavior. Partial failures are surfaced in `meta.engines_failed` and `meta.engine_errors`. If all selected engines fail, the endpoint returns a 502 with per-engine error
